label: Nova
note: Nova has 9 printed parts. The two paint entries (viewOnly, qty 0, no print file) exist only so the 3D viewer can show the visor's painted details in color: paint them onto the printed visor with acrylic paint pens. Nothing in them is printed.

parts.label: Body, arms, legs and boots
parts.supports: Tree supports under the two gloves and under the back edge of the torso behind the legs. None for the chest seat or the pocket.
parts.notes: Pause at 8 mm to swap to grey (#8c90a0) for the boots, or paint them; the gloves can be painted #e3dfd5. Press two M3 heat-set inserts into the 4.0 x 6.5 mm holes in the soles (x = +-12). The 7 mm cable channel runs from the sole up into the chest pocket, the 5 mm LED channel from the pocket up through the neck peg. The chest pocket is 22 x 22 x 15 mm behind the panel seat and centred on the cap axis (x = -5, z = 27); a module board up to 20 x 16 mm passes the 28 x 17 mm front window. About 64 x 36 x 49 mm.

parts.label: Helmet
parts.orientation: Flat seat down, visor toward the front of the bed
parts.supports: None needed. The roof of the visor pocket bridges about 6 mm. Tree supports are optional for the lowest 4 mm of the sphere beside the flat seat.
parts.notes: Thread the three wires of LED 1 through the 5 mm channel before gluing: it runs straight from the neck socket (10.4 x 6.5 mm, over the peg) to the antenna socket. Glue the helmet onto the collar and the peg, and the visor into the front pocket (0.2 mm clearance a side). A 62 mm sphere with its top at 99 mm.

parts.label: Visor
parts.notes: Print at 0.12 mm layers. Paint the raised eyes and smile ivory (#f3efe6) and the raised glint arc and dot lime (#d9ff3f). It is a plug: glue it into the helmet's visor pocket from the front.

parts.label: Collar ring
parts.notes: Slides over the neck peg and sits on the torso; the helmet rests on it. Extra part that gives the neck its suit-shade ring. Without it the helmet would leave a 3 mm gap.

parts.label: Backpack
parts.orientation: Lying on its back, glue face up
parts.notes: Glue the flat face onto the back of the torso, shifted to the viewer's left like the drawing. The upper edge is scooped to clear the helmet.

parts.label: Chest panel (bezel)
parts.orientation: Front up, flat back on the bed
parts.notes: Press the lime cap into the panel from behind, then glue the panel into the chest seat once the chest module is in the pocket (0.2 mm clearance a side). Paint the two raised bars panel-mark grey (#9d998f).

parts.label: Chest light cap (the button)
parts.notes: The 11 mm button: 0.3 mm clear in the panel's hole, with a 14 mm flange behind the lip so it cannot fall out and a 4 mm stem that presses the 6 x 6 mm switch. The stem tip stops 0.3 mm short of a 9.5 mm switch on a 1.6 mm board resting on the pocket's back wall. LED 0 sits beside the switch behind the flange.

parts.label: Antenna stalk
parts.orientation: Standing on the big plug, rod up
parts.supports: None. Use a brim: the rod is only 4 mm thick.
parts.notes: Thread the three 30 AWG wires of LED 1 through the 2.4 mm bore. The small plug glues into the helmet's antenna socket; the grey holder and the large plug carry the ball and put the LED board on the plug's end face.

parts.label: Antenna ball
parts.supports: None. The 11 mm dome inside bridges.
parts.notes: Hollow (inner 11 mm) for the 10 mm LED board of LED 1. Glue it over the board onto the stalk's plug through the 10.6 mm mouth.

parts.label: Paint: eyes and smile (ivory)
parts.notes: View only: a thin skin over the visor's raised eyes and smile, so the 3D viewer can show them in their paint color. Not printed. Paint the two raised eyes and the smile on nova_visor ivory (#f3efe6) with an acrylic paint pen, before the visor is glued into the helmet.

parts.label: Paint: glint arc and dot (lime)
parts.notes: View only: a thin skin over the visor's raised glints, so the 3D viewer can show them in their paint color. Not printed. Paint the raised glint arc at the upper left of the visor and the raised dot at the upper right on nova_visor lime (#d9ff3f) with an acrylic paint pen, before the visor is glued into the helmet.
